review_exclusions.endocrinolog-pseudohyperkalemia-due-to-t: wrong tier not clean: the patient does have the MPN (platelets 1.45M, palpable spleen), which CAUSES the gold pseudohyperkalemia; JAK2 is a defensible answer
review_exclusions.psychiatry-idiopathic-hypersomnia-ask_sy: wrong tier borderline: hypnagogic imagery in the prompt supports narcolepsy, which is a defensible co-diagnosis without a sleep study, and cataplexy is the standard question for any hypersomnia
review_exclusions.hepatology-mirizzi-syndrome-look_for_fin: the prompt spells out Mirizzi syndrome's defining anatomy (the audit notes it 'essentially defines' the diagnosis)
review_exclusions.nephrology-postpartum-lymphocytic-hypoph: the answer 'Failure of lactation' contradicts the prompt ('breastfeeding without difficulty')
review_exclusions.rheumatology-medial-epicondylitis-look_f: the prompt's 'recreational golfer ... medial elbow' lets a restating readout be credited for the alias golfer's elbow

gate: Qwen3.6-27B, chat template, enable_thinking=False. Answer probe (the prompt) and diagnosis probe (vignette + 'What is the most likely diagnosis?'): greedy in the modal class and >= 9/10 T=0.7 samples agree, both probes (Opus 5.5 equivalence judge). The diagnosis drives the answer: asked of the diagnosis alone (hop2) and with the diagnosis injected into the vignette, greedy + >= 8/10 samples give the same answer; injecting each of the two nearest differentials gives a different answer, and asked of each differential alone it gives a different answer too. No name, synonym or abbreviation of the target in the prompt (specific words of its name that occur are listed as leak_words and cleared by the auditor), and the answer does not name the target. Tier correct: diagnosis and answer equal the gold; tier wrong: a stable wrong diagnosis whose answer follows from it, and injecting the gold diagnosis yields the gold answer. Opus 5.5 audit: one clearly best diagnosis = gold (also named blind), standard answers, the model's diagnosis is a specific entity (wrong tier: distinct from gold and not defensible).
eval_render_note: EVAL RENDER: the `prompt` is the single user turn, rendered with the Qwen3.6 chat template, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=False. Read = EVERY token of that render (all prompt positions, the generation prompt included; offsets -n..-1, reply start = -1); never a response token.
read: every prompt position of the chat render (all_from_end)
targets: intermediates = a diagnosis the model did NOT use: the authored nearest differential (tier correct) or the missed gold (tier wrong); when that candidate overlaps anything Qwen wrote (a minority diagnosis sample naming the gold counts) the next differential is used instead (control_source = second_differential). Report control rates split by control_source. Items with no qualifying control, or whose control the prompt names, are omitted.

items.name: md-cardiology-syphilis-first_line_treatment
items.prompt: A 27-year-old man presents with bilateral red, photophobic eyes; slit-lamp exam shows patchy stromal interstitial keratitis. Over the past two weeks he has developed bilateral hearing loss, and a new early diastolic decrescendo murmur is heard at the left sternal border. The hearing loss was preceded by abrupt attacks of severe vertigo, tinnitus, and vomiting; his teeth and facial features are normal, RPR and FTA-ABS are negative, and ESR is 85 mm/h. What is the first-line treatment? Answer with just the treatment, nothing else.

items.name: md-gastroenterology-foreign-body-aspiration-first_line_treatment
items.prompt: A 2-year-old boy is brought in on an autumn evening with noisy breathing and coughing. The symptoms began abruptly while he was playing unsupervised; he is afebrile with no preceding runny nose, is drooling, and refuses solid food. A chest radiograph shows a round radiopaque disc seen face-on in the frontal view at the thoracic inlet. What is the first-line treatment? Answer with just the treatment, nothing else.

items.name: md-gastroenterology-intrahepatic-cholestasis-of-pregnancy-first_line_treatment
items.prompt: A 32-year-old woman 7 weeks after delivery presents with generalized pruritus, dark urine, and jaundice; ultrasound shows gallstones and sludge in the gallbladder, which were noted during pregnancy. The common bile duct measures 4 mm without visible stones, and she has no fever or right upper quadrant pain. She started a combined estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive 3 weeks ago and had severe itching with elevated bile acids in her third trimester that resolved after delivery. Labs show alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L, GGT 55 U/L, bilirubin 4.1 mg/dL, ALT 140 U/L, and normal lipase. What is the first-line treatment? Answer with just the treatment, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Discontinue the combined estrogen-containing contraceptive (switch to progestin-only or nonhormonal method)

items.name: md-gastroenterology-hirschsprung-disease-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 2-day-old term boy has progressive abdominal distension, bilious-tinged vomiting, and has not passed meconium since birth. He is macrosomic (4.6 kg), and his mother had poorly controlled pregestational diabetes treated with insulin. Rectal stimulation yields only a small amount of pale mucoid material, and an abdominal radiograph shows multiple dilated bowel loops without free air. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.

items.name: md-hematology-polycythemia-vera-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 26-year-old man has a ruddy complexion, occasional headaches, and a hemoglobin of 19.6 g/dL with hematocrit 58% on pre-employment testing. His father was told he had 'thick blood' and has undergone phlebotomies for years. Examination shows no splenomegaly, WBC and platelets are normal, SpO2 is 98%, and serum erythropoietin is upper-normal. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.

items.name: md-hepatology-wilson-disease-look_for_finding
items.prompt: A 15-year-old boy has declining school performance, clumsiness, slurred speech, and new psychiatric outbursts; ALT is 78 U/L and he has splenomegaly. Serum ceruloplasmin and 24-hour urinary copper are normal. He had prolonged jaundice as a newborn, and his parents describe episodes in which he suddenly goes limp and falls when laughing. If we can check for only one more physical exam finding, which finding should we look for? Answer with just the finding, nothing else.

items.name: md-pediatrics-lyme-disease-first_line_treatment
items.prompt: A 4-year-old girl from rural Montana developed an unsteady gait, then ascending weakness of the legs and arms over about 24 hours; she had a mild cold 2 weeks ago. She is afebrile, with symmetric flaccid weakness, absent deep tendon reflexes, and normal sensation. CSF cell count and protein are normal. Parting her thick hair reveals a firm, engorged arthropod firmly attached to the scalp behind the left ear. What is the first-line treatment? Answer with just the treatment, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Complete removal of the attached tick

items.name: md-rheumatology-intrahepatic-cholestasis-of-pregnancy-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 34-year-old woman with dry eyes, dry mouth and positive anti-Ro antibodies presents at 30 weeks' gestation with generalized pruritus worst on the palms and soles at night, with excoriations but no primary rash. Alkaline phosphatase is 4 times the pregnancy-adjusted upper limit, GGT is elevated and aminotransferases are mildly raised. She recalls itching and an elevated GGT at a check-up 2 years before this pregnancy, and the itching persisted for months after her previous delivery. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.

items.name: md-rheumatology-familial-mediterranean-fever-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 24-year-old man of Turkish ancestry has had recurrent febrile attacks since childhood with severe abdominal pain, pleuritic chest pain and markedly raised CRP; colchicine 2 mg/day has not reduced their frequency. Each attack lasts 2-3 weeks and is accompanied by a painful erythematous patch that migrates down a limb over tender underlying muscle, plus periorbital swelling. His father and paternal aunt have similar episodes. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.

items.name: md-rheumatology-giant-cell-arteritis-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 71-year-old woman presents with 10 days of severe, boring right periorbital and temporal headache and double vision; ESR is 48 mm/h. Exam shows right ptosis and limitation of adduction, elevation, depression, and abduction of the right eye, with reduced sensation over the right forehead, while visual acuity and fundi are normal. Temporal arteries are non-tender with normal pulses and she denies jaw claudication or shoulder stiffness. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Contrast-enhanced MRI of the cavernous sinus and orbit

items.name: md-allergy-and-immu-kawasaki-disease-first_line_treatment
items.prompt: A 4-year-old boy has had 5 days of high fever, irritability, bilateral nonexudative conjunctival injection, and swelling of his hands and feet, with a rash that now involves the palms and soles. The rash began as blanching macules on the wrists and ankles, spread centrally, and is now becoming petechial. He went camping in North Carolina 8 days before the fever began. Labs show platelets of 70,000/µL and sodium of 128 mEq/L. What is the first-line treatment? Answer with just the treatment, nothing else.

items.name: md-cardiology-pheochromocytoma-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 42-year-old woman reports 6 months of pounding headaches, palpitations, and sweating, and her BP is 178/104 despite amlodipine and lisinopril; she also notes muscle weakness and nocturia. She takes no diuretics; potassium is 2.9 mEq/L, bicarbonate 33 mEq/L, and sodium 144 mEq/L. CT shows a 1.4 cm left adrenal nodule with an unenhanced attenuation of 4 Hounsfield units. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Plasma aldosterone-to-renin ratio (followed by saline suppression testing)

items.name: md-critical-care-alcoholic-ketoacidosis-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 66-year-old man with heavy daily alcohol use was admitted to the ICU 4 days ago for severe withdrawal and has required a continuous lorazepam infusion, now 15 mg/h. He has received thiamine and dextrose-containing fluids since admission. Today he has a new anion gap metabolic acidosis (bicarbonate 13 mmol/L, anion gap 24) with a modestly elevated lactate and rising creatinine, but he is hemodynamically stable without signs of infection. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Serum osmolal gap (measured minus calculated osmolality) or serum propylene glycol level

items.name: md-dermatology-scabies-look_for_finding
items.prompt: A 70-year-old homeless man has had intense itching for 1 month that is worse at night, and other men at his shelter are also itchy. Exam shows excoriated papules with hemorrhagic puncta and lichenified hyperpigmented skin concentrated on the upper back, shoulders, and waistband area. His finger webs, wrists, and genitals are spared, and he has worn the same clothes for weeks. If we can check for only one more physical exam finding, which finding should we look for? Answer with just the finding, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Lice and nits in the seams of clothing

items.name: md-dermatology-scurvy-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 23-year-old woman at 15 weeks' gestation presents with new bruising on her arms and legs, gum bleeding when brushing, and a nosebleed. She has had severe vomiting since 6 weeks' gestation requiring repeated admissions, has eaten almost nothing for 2 months, and recently completed a 3-week course of broad-spectrum antibiotics. Exam shows large ecchymoses on her limbs and a few petechiae on her shins, with no lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Prothrombin time/INR (prolonged, correcting after vitamin K)

items.name: md-geriatrics-vasovagal-syncope-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 12-year-old girl briefly lost consciousness at the end of a hot outdoor running race; she felt lightheaded beforehand, recovered within a minute, and her mother faints at blood draws. Further history reveals a second episode during a heated argument with her brother. A cousin died suddenly at age 15 while playing sports, and her resting ECG (normal QTc) and echocardiogram are normal. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Exercise stress test showing exercise-induced bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular ectopy/tachycardia

items.name: md-infectious-disea-scabies-look_for_finding
items.prompt: A 50-year-old homeless man presents with several weeks of intense generalized itching. Examination shows linear excoriations, small red puncta, and hyperpigmented thickened skin over the shoulders, upper back, and waistline. The scalp and pubic hair appear clear. If we can check for only one more physical exam finding, which finding should we look for? Answer with just the finding, nothing else.
items.target: Burrows in the finger web spaces
items.correct_answer: Lice and nits in the seams of clothing

items.name: md-obstetrics-eclampsia-first_line_treatment
items.prompt: A 26-year-old primigravida at 41 weeks has a sudden generalized tonic-clonic seizure 20 hours into an induction of labor, after 2 hours of headache, nausea, and vomiting. Her BP is 128/80, the urine dipstick is negative for protein, reflexes are normal, and platelets and liver enzymes are normal. What is the first-line treatment? Answer with just the treatment, nothing else.

items.name: md-ophthalmology-neuromyelitis-optica-spectrum-disorder-confirm_test
items.prompt: A 9-year-old boy develops painful vision loss in both eyes to 20/200 over 3 days, 2 weeks after a viral illness. Both optic discs are markedly swollen. Which single test would best confirm the diagnosis? Answer with just the test, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Serum MOG-IgG by live cell-based assay

items.name: md-pulmonology-opioid-overdose-first_line_treatment
items.prompt: A 28-year-old woman is drowsy 8 hours after cesarean delivery for severe hypertension in pregnancy, with a respiratory rate of 7/min and SpO2 of 86%. She received IV morphine for incisional pain an hour ago and is on a continuous IV infusion started before surgery. Her pupils are 4 mm and reactive, and patellar reflexes are absent. Urine output has been 10 mL/h, and her creatinine has doubled. What is the first-line treatment? Answer with just the treatment, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: IV calcium gluconate and stop the magnesium infusion

items.name: md-urology-fournier-gangrene-look_for_finding
items.prompt: A 68-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes was diagnosed 8 days ago with a febrile urinary tract infection and perineal pain and has been treated with culture-appropriate ciprofloxacin. He remains febrile to 39.2°C with persistent perineal pain, and he has developed urinary retention requiring a catheter. Blood and urine cultures are now sterile. If we can check for only one more physical exam finding, which finding should we look for? Answer with just the finding, nothing else.
items.correct_answer: Fluctuant area on digital rectal exam

items.name: md-orthopedics-sickle-cell-disease-confirm_test

items.name: md-emergency-medici-sigmoid-volvulus-first_line_treatment

items.name: md-allergy-and-immu-allergic-bronchopulmonary-aspergillosis-watch_complication

items.name: md-allergy-and-immu-chronic-granulomatous-disease-confirm_test

items.name: md-cardiology-coarctation-of-the-aorta-look_for_finding

items.name: md-cardiology-pulmonary-embolism-confirm_test

items.name: md-cardiology-stable-angina-confirm_test

items.name: md-cardiology-vasospastic-angina-first_line_treatment

items.name: md-critical-care-wernicke-encephalopathy-first_line_treatment

What is the first-line treatment? Answer with just the treatment, nothing else.

items.name: md-dermatology-vitiligo-watch_complication

items.name: md-emergency-medici-boerhaave-syndrome-confirm_test

Serum calcium is 11.3 mg/dL on two occasions, phosphate 2.2 mg/dL, with normal albumin and creatinine. She has no weight loss or other systemic symptoms. items.name: md-gastroenterology-hepatitis-c-associated-mixed-cryoglobulinemia-look_for_finding
